cards.title: Filtering & NULL
cards.summary: SQL uses three-valued logic: NULL is unknown, not an ordinary value.

entries.meaning: Normal scalar comparisons.
Inclusive lower and upper bounds.
Match any listed value.
% = any run, _ = one character.
Use IS NULL / IS NOT NULL, never = NULL.
Parenthesize mixed AND/OR expressions.

more.meaning: A NULL in the subquery/list can make the predicate unknown; NOT EXISTS is usually safer.
more.detail: WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM blocked b WHERE b.user_id = u.id)

more.meaning: Replace NULL only when that semantic replacement is intended.
more.detail: COALESCE(phone, 'missing')

cards.title: Aggregation
cards.summary: Aggregate functions collapse multiple input rows into one result per group.

entries.meaning: Count rows, including rows whose columns contain NULL.
Count non-NULL values in one expression.
Count unique non-NULL values.
Total or mean of non-NULL numeric values.
Smallest or largest non-NULL value.
Filter aggregate groups, not source rows.

more.meaning: Turn a condition into a numeric contribution.
more.detail: SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'paid' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)

more.meaning: Aggregate only matching rows.
more.detail: SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'paid' THEN total ELSE 0 END)

cards.title: Joins
cards.summary: Choose the join from the row-preservation requirement, then verify cardinality.

entries.meaning: Keep only matching rows from both sides.
entries.detail: FROM users u JOIN orders o ON o.user_id = u.id

entries.meaning: Keep every left row; unmatched right columns become NULL.
entries.detail: FROM users u LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.user_id = u.id

entries.meaning: Cartesian product; useful intentionally, dangerous accidentally.
Join on the complete business/key relationship.
entries.detail: ON a.tenant_id = b.tenant_id AND a.id = b.id

entries.meaning: A parent repeats once per matching child.
entries.detail: COUNT(*) may grow after a join

entries.meaning: A right-side WHERE condition can effectively turn LEFT JOIN into INNER JOIN.
entries.detail: Put match-only condition in ON when left rows must survive

more.meaning: Anti-join pattern.
more.detail: LEFT JOIN orders o ON … WHERE o.id IS NULL

more.meaning: Often clearer than joining only to test existence.
more.detail: WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders o WHERE o.user_id = u.id)

cards.title: Set operations
cards.summary: Combine compatible result sets vertically; column counts and compatible types must align.

entries.meaning: Combine and remove duplicates.
entries.detail: SELECT email FROM leads UNION SELECT email FROM users

entries.meaning: Combine and preserve duplicates; usually cheaper than UNION.
entries.detail: SELECT id FROM a UNION ALL SELECT id FROM b

entries.meaning: Rows present in both results where supported.
entries.detail: SELECT id FROM a INTERSECT SELECT id FROM b

entries.meaning: Rows in the first result but not the second where supported.
entries.detail: SELECT id FROM expected EXCEPT SELECT id FROM actual

cards.title: Subqueries & EXISTS
cards.summary: Use scalar subqueries for one value and EXISTS when the question is whether a related row exists.

entries.meaning: Subquery must return at most one row/value.
Compare against a one-column result set.
entries.detail: WHERE user_id IN (SELECT id FROM vip_users)

entries.meaning: True as soon as a correlated match exists.
entries.detail: WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders o WHERE o.user_id = u.id)

entries.meaning: Robust anti-match pattern, including NULL-sensitive cases.
entries.detail: WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders o WHERE o.user_id = u.id)

entries.meaning: Inner query refers to the current outer row.

cards.title: CTEs
cards.summary: Name intermediate result sets to make multi-step SQL easier to reason about and test.

entries.meaning: Define a named result for the following statement.
entries.detail: WITH paid AS (SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = 'paid') SELECT * FROM paid

entries.meaning: Chain readable stages separated by commas.
entries.detail: WITH a AS (…), b AS (SELECT … FROM a) SELECT … FROM b

entries.meaning: Optionally name CTE output columns explicitly.

cards.title: CASE, COALESCE & CAST
cards.summary: Small expressions that make reporting and validation queries far more useful.

entries.meaning: Conditional expression.
entries.detail: CASE WHEN score >= 80 THEN 'high' ELSE 'other' END

entries.meaning: First non-NULL expression.
Return NULL when two expressions are equal; handy for safe division.
Convert to a target SQL type.

cards.title: Window ranking
cards.summary: Windows calculate across related rows without collapsing them like GROUP BY does.

entries.meaning: Unique sequence inside each partition; ties still receive different numbers.
entries.detail: ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY created_at DESC)

entries.meaning: Ties share rank and leave gaps.
Ties share rank without gaps.
Rank inside a CTE/subquery, then filter the generated rank outside.
entries.detail: WITH x AS (SELECT …, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC) rn FROM …) SELECT * FROM x WHERE rn = 1

cards.title: Window analysis
cards.summary: Running totals, comparisons with adjacent rows, and partition-level statistics.

entries.meaning: Accumulate in deterministic order.
entries.detail: SUM(total) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY created_at, id ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING)

entries.meaning: Aggregate per partition while retaining detail rows.
Read a previous row's value in window order.
entries.detail: LAG(total) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY created_at)

entries.meaning: Read a following row's value.
entries.detail: LEAD(created_at) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY created_at)

entries.meaning: Explicit ROWS frame avoids surprising peer/range behavior.
entries.detail: AVG(total) OVER (ORDER BY day ROWS BETWEEN 6 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)

cards.title: INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE
cards.summary: For destructive statements, prove the target rows with SELECT first and use transactions when appropriate.

entries.meaning: Insert explicit columns; avoid relying on table column order.
Insert a query result.
entries.detail: INSERT INTO archive (id, email) SELECT id, email FROM users WHERE status = 'inactive'

entries.meaning: Change matching rows; verify the WHERE predicate first.
entries.detail: UPDATE users SET status = 'inactive' WHERE last_login < '2025-01-01'

entries.meaning: Remove matching rows; missing WHERE means all rows.
entries.detail: DELETE FROM sessions WHERE expires_at < CURRENT_TIMESTAMP

more.meaning: Run the same predicate as SELECT before a destructive change.
more.detail: SELECT id FROM users WHERE …

more.meaning: Treat row count as evidence: unexpectedly high or zero counts deserve investigation.
more.detail: Compare expected vs actual affected-row count

cards.title: Tables & constraints
cards.summary: Constraints make invalid states impossible at the database boundary instead of merely unlikely.

entries.meaning: Unique, non-NULL row identity.
Require referenced parent data.
Reject duplicate key combinations under engine NULL semantics.
Reject missing values.
Enforce a row-level predicate where supported/enforced.
Value used when the column is omitted.

more.meaning: Change schema; supported operations differ substantially by engine/version.
more.detail: ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN locale VARCHAR(10)

more.meaning: Destructive schema change; dependency behavior is engine-specific.
more.detail: DROP TABLE old_table

cards.title: Transactions
cards.summary: Group dependent writes so they commit together or roll back together; begin syntax varies slightly by engine.

entries.meaning: Explicit transaction block.
Explicit transaction block for transactional storage engines.
Begin a transaction; locking mode can be qualified.
T-SQL transaction block.
Create a partial rollback point inside a transaction.
T-SQL uses SAVE TRANSACTION and ROLLBACK TRANSACTION.
entries.detail: SAVE TRANSACTION before_step; … ROLLBACK TRANSACTION before_step

more.meaning: Test lost updates, non-repeatable reads, phantoms, and serialization behavior according to the configured level.
more.detail: READ COMMITTED / REPEATABLE READ / SERIALIZABLE / engine variants

cards.title: Indexes & EXPLAIN
cards.summary: Indexes are workload-specific. Verify plans and timings instead of assuming an index makes a query faster.

entries.meaning: Common B-tree index for selective lookup/order patterns.
entries.detail: CREATE INDEX idx_orders_user_created ON orders (user_id, created_at)

entries.meaning: Column order matters; align it with real predicates/orderings.
Inspect planner output; ANALYZE executes the statement.
Inspect access path/plan.
Inspect high-level query plan.
Use actual/estimated execution plans in SSMS or SET SHOWPLAN options.

more.meaning: Functions/transforms on indexed columns can prevent efficient seeks in many cases.
more.detail: Prefer created_at >= boundary over DATE(created_at) = … when possible

more.meaning: Compare realistic data volumes, warm/cold effects, row counts, and plan changes.
more.detail: Plan + latency + rows + I/O evidence

cards.title: QA data checks
cards.summary: Compact queries for validating uniqueness, completeness, referential integrity, and reconciliation.

entries.meaning: Find keys that occur more than once.
entries.detail: SELECT external_id, COUNT(*) c FROM t GROUP BY external_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 1

entries.meaning: Find unexpected NULLs/blanks.
entries.detail: SELECT * FROM t WHERE email IS NULL OR TRIM(email) = ''

entries.meaning: Find children without a parent.
entries.detail: SELECT c.* FROM child c LEFT JOIN parent p ON p.id = c.parent_id WHERE p.id IS NULL

entries.meaning: Compare independently computed aggregates at the same grain.
Surface values outside an allowed set.
entries.detail: SELECT status, COUNT(*) FROM t GROUP BY status

entries.meaning: Check latest expected event/load time.

more.meaning: Compare source/target counts, but pair counts with key/value reconciliation.
more.detail: expected_count - actual_count

more.meaning: Inspect first/last/min/max values around time and numeric boundaries.
more.detail: MIN(), MAX(), ORDER BY … FETCH/LIMIT

cards.title: Limit & pagination by dialect
cards.summary: Always pair pagination with deterministic ORDER BY. The row-limiting syntax is not uniform.

entries.meaning: LIMIT/OFFSET is common; FETCH is also supported.
LIMIT with OFFSET.
LIMIT with OFFSET.
TOP for simple limits; OFFSET/FETCH for paging requires ORDER BY.
entries.detail: ORDER BY id OFFSET 40 ROWS FETCH NEXT 20 ROWS ONLY

more.meaning: For deep/stable paging, compare from the last seen ordered key instead of large OFFSETs.
more.detail: WHERE created_at < :last_created OR (created_at = :last_created AND id < :last_id) ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC

cards.title: Upsert & changed rows
cards.summary: Conflict handling and returning changed rows are vendor-specific—keep them isolated from portable SQL.

entries.meaning: Handle a unique/exclusion conflict with ON CONFLICT.
entries.detail: INSERT INTO users(id,email) VALUES (1,'a@x') ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE SET email = EXCLUDED.email

entries.meaning: SQLite also supports ON CONFLICT upsert syntax.
entries.detail: INSERT INTO users(id,email) VALUES (1,'a@x') ON CONFLICT(id) DO UPDATE SET email = excluded.email

entries.meaning: Use ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE for duplicate unique/primary keys.
entries.detail: INSERT INTO users(id,email) VALUES (1,'a@x') ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE email = 'a@x'

entries.meaning: RETURNING can return inserted/updated/deleted values.
entries.detail: INSERT INTO users(email) VALUES ('a@x') RETURNING id

entries.meaning: Modern SQLite supports RETURNING on top-level DML.
entries.detail: UPDATE users SET active = 0 WHERE id = 1 RETURNING id

entries.meaning: OUTPUT exposes inserted/deleted pseudo-tables.
entries.detail: UPDATE users SET active = 0 OUTPUT inserted.id WHERE id = 1

more.meaning: MERGE exists but has complex concurrency/trigger semantics; validate the chosen pattern for the workload.
more.detail: MERGE is T-SQL-specific; test behavior under concurrent writes

cards.title: Date/time by dialect
cards.summary: Date arithmetic is one of the fastest places for otherwise-portable SQL to diverge.

entries.meaning: Interval arithmetic.
DATE_ADD / DATE_SUB family.
Date/time functions use modifier strings.
DATEADD / DATEDIFF family.
Store/compare timestamps at a clear timezone/precision and test boundary conversions explicitly.
entries.detail: UTC instant vs local business date are different concepts

cards.title: String aggregation by dialect
cards.summary: Basic string functions overlap, but aggregating many rows into one string uses different names.

entries.meaning: Aggregate strings with a delimiter.
GROUP_CONCAT supports ordering/separators.
group_concat is the native name; current SQLite also documents string_agg as an alias.
STRING_AGG combines rows; ordering uses WITHIN GROUP.
